# Ball joints, tie rods and steering linkage

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Install a new manual hub assembly by transferring axle components and setting it to free mode. [t2130]

Inspect and check components to prevent stress failure or bending forces on stock links. [t2303]

[Partial] Remove wheel and disconnect knuckle from upper post, then install new joints. [t1763]

[Partial] Remove castle nut from upper ball joint, unbolt lower shock mount for clearance. [t1905]

Source a late model Pathfinder front upper ball joint to replace one on an AC 3-inch suspension lift. [t1766]

[Partial] Check the ball joints before driving and inspect the camper bolts for looseness. [t1381]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Lift the front end by jacking up the rear tires to gain clearance.
2. Remove both front wheels from the vehicle.
3. Locate and remove six small bolts securing the auto hub housing using a size 6 Allen key, ensuring a perfect fit to prevent stripping.
4. Remove the original auto hub assembly and extract its C-clip by placing it on the ground or using two flat-head screwdrivers if necessary.
5. Transfer any remaining components locked in place by the C-clip from the axle shaft to the ground as they are not needed for manual hubs.
6. Install the top portion of the new manual hub onto the axle, ensuring there is a correct number of splines and it fits snugly.
7. [Partial] Apply packing grease generously to the internal moving parts of the new hub assembly.
8. Reinstall the six size 6 Allen bolts that hold the housing firmly against the axle shaft.
9. Attach the dial piece or lever mechanism that allows spinning the hub between free-wheeling and locked positions.
10. Set the manual hub into 'free' mode to ensure smooth rotation before final tightening.

_Procedure reported by [t2130]._

1. [Partial] Inspect the center link for stress failure at the adjuster point.
2. Check if the upper and lower arms are bent or broken due to bending forces.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1763] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the wheel to access the ball joint.
2. Disconnect the knuckle from the upper ball joint post.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1905] [Partial]</summary>

1. Remove the castle nut from the upper ball joint.
2. Unbolt the lower mount for the shock absorber to create clearance.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1766] [Partial]</summary>

1. Identify the need for a replacement ball joint on an AC 3-inch suspension lift control arm.
2. Source a late model Pathfinder front upper ball joint instead of waiting for specialty parts.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1381] [Partial]</summary>

1. Check the ball joints before driving anywhere.
2. [Partial] Inspect the camber bolts to ensure they are not loose.

</details>

## Parts

- C-clip, retaining clip: Used on the original auto hub but often transferred or discarded for manual setups. [t2130]
- Center Link: OEM style, stock center link [t2303]
- [Partial] Manual hub assembly: Often referred to as 'Hardbody' style, requiring fewer splines than auto hubs. [t2130]
- [Partial] Tie Rod Ends, TRA: Heavy Duty Trail Rated or upgraded steel version [t2303]

## Specifications

- **Lower ball joint nut torque**: 118-191 [t1763] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Upper ball joint nut torque**: 78-147 [t1763] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Wheel lug torque**: 80-100 [t1763] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use 'Lock-Tite' thread locker on the six housing bolts, as standard lock washers may still back out due to heat. [t2130]
- Consider replacing the supplied studs with cap screws (socket head) if you want a more reliable connection. [t2130]
- Note that the bending forces occur in the middle of the link at the adjuster. [t2303]
- Better steel is preferred to resist force and prevent deformation. [t2303]
- [Partial] Use a press to install the ball joint if space is tight. [t1763]
- Consider using a tie rod puller instead of disassembling the hub and CV axle. [t1763]
- Use a propane bottle torch to heat stuck hardware if mechanical force fails. [t1905]
- Strike the knuckle area where the ball joint passes through with a hammer and beat it until vibration loosens it. [t1905]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Stripping one of the small size 6 Allen bolts by using an ill-fitting key. [t2130]
- Allowing the C-clip to pop back into place prematurely while removing other components. [t2130]
- [Partial] Servicing a stock center link by replacing ball joints individually, as the design itself may be weak for larger tires. [t2303]
- [Partial] Using standard length tie rod ends with a Calimini kit without accounting for longer adjusters. [t2303]
- Struggling with lower ball joint removal due to limited space for the socket. [t1763]
